question: What is the name of the parasite that causes Guinea worm disease?
explanation: Dracunculus medinensis is the specific roundworm responsible for causing Guinea worm disease in humans. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h1)

question: How do people usually catch a Guinea worm infection?

options.C: Ingesting water containing infected water fleas

explanation: Infective larvae live inside tiny water fleas (copepods) found in stagnant water sources, and enter the body when swallowed. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h1)

question: Where do female Guinea worms usually travel to inside the body before coming out through the skin?

options.A: The brain and central nervous system
options.C: The skin of the lower limbs

explanation: Mature female worms migrate toward the skin surface, most commonly the legs and feet, to release their larvae into water. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h2)

question: What happens to the infected water fleas once a human swallows them?

options.A: They pass through the digestive tract unharmed
options.B: They burrow directly through the stomach lining
options.C: Stomach acid kills them and frees the larvae
options.D: They multiply rapidly inside the small intestine

explanation: Stomach acid destroys the water flea, releasing the infective larvae so they can penetrate the intestinal wall. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h2)

question: Which water source has the highest risk of spreading Guinea worm disease?
explanation: Stagnant surface water allows water fleas to thrive and makes it easy for infected people to contaminate the supply. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h3)

question: Why do infected individuals often place their affected leg into a water source?

options.A: To soften the skin for medicated creams
options.B: To help wash away wound discharge
options.C: To relieve the intense burning pain caused by the worm
options.D: To encourage the entire worm to fall out quickly

explanation: The emerging worm causes a severe burning sensation, prompting the patient to soak the limb in water, which causes the worm to release its larvae. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h3)

question: What is the very first sign that a Guinea worm is about to emerge?

options.A: An intense burning sensation and painful blister
options.C: A dark purple bruise without surface changes
options.D: Numbness and coldness in the foot

explanation: Patients experience severe localized burning and itching right before a blister forms over the spot where the worm will exit. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h4)

question: How long does it usually take for symptoms to appear after getting infected with a Guinea worm?
explanation: The parasite takes nearly a year to mature and move through the body before any signs of infection show up. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h4)

question: What is the standard method used to remove an emerging Guinea worm?

options.A: Surgically cutting out the entire worm
options.B: Gradually rolling the worm around a small stick each day
options.C: Injecting anti-parasitic drugs directly into the blister
options.D: Applying heat to force the worm out instantly

explanation: Slow mechanical extraction over several days prevents the fragile worm from breaking inside the skin tissue. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h5)

question: What complication happens if a Guinea worm is pulled out too fast and breaks?

options.A: The remaining worm travels to the brain
options.C: The wound heals immediately without issues

explanation: Breaking the worm leaves decomposing parts inside the tissue, which triggers a strong immune reaction and secondary infections. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h5)

question: What is the main reason for isolating people with active Guinea worm blisters?

options.A: To ensure they take their oral antibiotics
options.B: To protect them from catching airborne diseases
options.C: To prevent them from contaminating community drinking water
options.D: To stop the worms from spreading directly from person to person

explanation: Isolating infected individuals stops them from soaking their sores in ponds, which breaks the transmission cycle of the parasite. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a standard nursing intervention for controlling Guinea worm disease?

options.A: Distributing fine-mesh cloth filters for water
options.B: Searching for active cases in rural areas
options.C: Educating residents to boil drinking water
options.D: Giving a routine preventive vaccine to infants

explanation: There is currently no vaccine available for Guinea worm disease, so water filtration and health education remain the main ways to control it. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h6)
